nodes.title: 分离 H3 音视频潜空间

widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the woman shown in <Picture 1>. Preserve her identity, facial structure, skin tone, hairstyle, clothing, accessories, body proportions, seated or standing posture, and all other recognizable visual characteristics exactly as shown in the source image.
<Subject 2> is the guitar held by <Subject 1> in <Picture 1>. Preserve its type, shape, color, material, strings, fretboard, orientation, scale, and position relative to the woman's body.
<Picture 1> is the exact first frame and composition anchor of [Shot 1], defining the woman's appearance and pose, the guitar position, hand placement, framing, camera viewpoint, background, lighting, color, and spatial relationships.
<Audio 1> is the complete synchronized singing-and-guitar performance for <Subject 1> (S1). It is directly reused as the target video's complete final audio track.

summary:
[keyframe completion + reference generation + audio reuse] The target video begins exactly from <Picture 1> and shows <Subject 1> naturally playing <Subject 2> while physically singing the complete vocal performance contained in <Audio 1>. Her mouth, facial expressions, breathing, strumming or picking hand, and fretboard hand movements remain precisely synchronized with the reused audio. The scene is presented as one continuous shot with subtle handheld camera movement.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the woman's identity, facial features, hairstyle, clothing, accessories, body proportions, and overall appearance remain consistent with <Picture 1>.
<Subject 2> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the guitar's appearance, proportions, orientation, and physical relationship with the woman remain consistent with <Picture 1>.
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the video begins exactly from the supplied image, preserving its initial composition, pose, subject placement, guitar position, camera angle, background, and lighting.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - the complete source signal is copied 1:1 and used as the target video's sole final audio track, preserving its original duration, timing, vocals, guitar performance, pauses, breathing, room tone, loudness, and all existing audible details.

detailed_description:
The target video uses a photorealistic, intimate live-performance style with natural facial animation, physically accurate guitar playing, stable character identity, and consistent scene details. It is presented as one uninterrupted shot.

[Shot 1] The video begins exactly from <Picture 1>. <Subject 1> (S1) and <Subject 2> remain in the precise opening pose, position, scale, orientation, and framing established by the first frame. Preserve the woman's face, hairstyle, clothing, accessories, body proportions, and posture. Preserve the guitar's shape, color, material, fretboard, strings, orientation, and contact with her body. The original background, lighting direction, shadows, depth of field, and color balance remain visually consistent throughout the shot.

As <Audio 1> begins, <Subject 1> (S1) naturally starts playing the guitar and physically singing the exact vocal content already present in the reused audio. Her lips, jaw, cheeks, and throat move in precise synchronization with the original syllables, sustained notes, phrasing, rhythm, emotional delivery, breaths, and pauses. Her mouth remains naturally relaxed whenever the vocal layer is silent.

Her guitar performance follows <Audio 1> accurately. The strumming or picking hand moves in time with every audible stroke and rhythmic accent, while the fretboard hand forms plausible chord shapes and changes position naturally according to the harmonic progression. Finger motion remains anatomically correct and temporally stable. The hands maintain believable contact with the strings, neck, and body of the guitar without drifting or changing shape.

The woman's upper body responds subtly to the performance through gentle breathing, small shoulder movement, restrained head motion, occasional natural blinking, slight changes in eye direction, and expressive but controlled facial reactions. Her emotion follows the intensity and phrasing of the singing without exaggerated gestures. Her identity, facial geometry, hands, guitar, clothing, and background remain consistent throughout the complete video.

The camera maintains the composition established by <Picture 1> while shaking slightly with very small amplitude at slow speed, resembling restrained handheld breathing from a nearby camera operator. The movement is smooth, irregular, and subtle rather than rhythmic. The camera does not change its focal length or substantially alter the framing.

The performance continues for the full duration of <Audio 1>. The final mouth movement, guitar stroke, and hand motion finish precisely with the corresponding final sounds. The woman then settles naturally while the final frame remains stable.

overall_soundscape:
<Audio 1> is directly reused as the sole and complete final audio track. The audible singing, guitar performance, breathing, room tone, and all other existing sound details remain exactly synchronized with the visible performance.

N/A

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> (S1) is JackeyLove, whose facial identity, facial proportions, eyes, nose, mouth, jawline, hairstyle, skin tone, age, and body proportions come exclusively from <Picture 2>. His TES jersey, microphone, pose, framing, stage, and lighting come from <Picture 1>; <Picture 1> contributes no facial identity.
<Picture 1> is the main opening composition and performance-layout reference.
<Picture 2> is the exclusive facial-identity reference for <Subject 1>.
<Audio 1> is the supplied original master-song segment and must be copied 1:1, sample-for-sample, as the complete and only final audio track.

summary:
[reference generation + keyframe completion + audio reuse] The target video animates <Picture 1>, replaces its depicted performer with the recognizable JackeyLove identity from <Picture 2>, and synchronizes singing and movement to <Audio 1>. No reference video is used.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (all shots): fully_preserved - JackeyLove remains recognizably identical to <Picture 2> at every angle.
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] opening composition): partially_preserved - microphone, jersey, pose, framing and stage are retained while the face is governed exclusively by <Picture 2>.
<Picture 2> (identity): fully_preserved - recognizable facial structure and hairstyle are retained.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - the complete supplied waveform, vocals, lyrics, melody, harmony, instrumentation, tempo, duration, dynamics, and mix are copied unchanged as the target video's only audio track.

detailed_description:
Live-action cinematic 16:9 traditional-rock performance on the same black-red stage. [Shot 1] The frame begins from the composition of <Picture 1>. <Subject 1> (S1) appears recognizably identical to JackeyLove in <Picture 2>, in a chest-up frontal dolly shot with both eyes and the complete mouth unobstructed. He sings exactly with <Audio 1>, using phoneme-accurate lip shapes, jaw motion, breath timing, and restrained cold, mocking expression. [Shot 2] At 00:02.700, after a lyric phrase ends, the shot hard-cuts to a three-quarter profile with the microphone grille in the foreground; a short rack focus moves from the grille to his eyes and mouth. [Shot 3] At 00:05.400, a snare accent cuts to a waist-up lateral tracking shot that briefly reveals the guitarist behind him while his mouth remains readable. No invented words, no exaggerated gestures, and no identity drift.

overall_soundscape:
No additional ambience, Foley, crowd noise, or sound effects are generated; only <Audio 1> is audible.

non_diegetic_music:
<Audio 1> is copied unchanged as the sole music track. No new music, remix, extension, replacement, variation, or additional score is generated.
